Weak trade wind showers have been slow to arrive and will now bring 
scattered showers to the northern CNMI this evening and to Guam and 
Rota after midnight before dropping back down to isolated for the 
rest of the forecast period. The potential for lighter winds by mid 
next week may allow for some island effect showers to develop but 
this remains uncertain.

Marine...
Models and surf observations show that combined seas are 3 to 5 feet
and will remain so through the weekend. There is a moderate risk of 
rip currents through at least Sunday night for east and west facing 
reefs and a low risk for north and south facing reefs. The main 
swells are a persistent east trade swell, a southwest swell from TS 
Jangmi, and a lingering weak northeast swell. Light to gentle 
easterly winds are expected to continue through Monday before 
possibly decreasing Tuesday.

Eastern Micronesia...
Satellite shows partly cloudy skies with spotty showers across
Kosrae and Majuro this afternoon, and mostly cloudy skies with
scattered showers across Pohnpei. Extensive cloudiness with numerous
showers are seen well east through south of Majuro. 

A Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) is currently in place across eastern
Micronesia from south of Pohnpei to Kosrae to beyond the Date Line
near 5N. This will be the main weather producer across the region 
for the next few days. Strong upper-level convergence is currently 
in place from just east of Pohnpei to Majuro, resulting in only 
patchy clouds and spotty showers over both Kosrae and Majuro this 
afternoon. Borderline scattered showers and the potential for
isolated thunderstorms are seen over Pohnpei, mostly over the 
western waters. Through the evening, the convergence aloft looks to 
begin to erode, allowing increased convection over Pohnpei Sunday 
through Monday afternoon and over Kosrae Sunday through Monday night.
A couple of weak trade-wind troughs approaching the region will 
enhance the convergence along the NET, allowing POPs (Probability of 
Precipitation) to climb up to around 40 percent Sunday and Sunday 
night. By Monday night at Pohnpei and Tuesday at Kosrae, expect the 
NET to weaken significantly as it drifts south, allowing a dry 
pattern to move into both locations and persist through at least the 
middle of next week. For Majuro, expect the atoll to remain fairly 
dry tonight through Sunday night until a weak circulation along the 
NET pushes west of the Date Line and increases convection across the 
Marshalls Monday through Tuesday. As the NET weakens and drifts 
south, expect a drying pattern across Majuro by the middle of next 
week.

Light to gentle winds and benign seas are expected to continue across
the region through most of next week.

Western Micronesia...
To the distant northwest, TS Jangmi continues to steer monsoon
southwesterly winds across much of Palau and across Yap Proper this
afternoon. Scattered to numerous showers continue tonight, with locally
heavy showers and occasional gusts to 25 kt remaining possible at 
Palau. As Jangmi continues to move northwest, an area of high 
pressure between the monsoon pattern and a NET disturbance near 
Chuuk, is expected to move closer to Yap Proper and Palau. This 
transition away from the monsoon flow will yield light and variable 
winds overnight at Yap and starting Sunday night at Palau. Showers
look to gradually diminish, becoming isolated to low-end scattered 
Sunday night. Latest model guidance depicts convection loosely 
organized around the nearby NET pattern to the east which looks to 
bring periods of scattered showers for Yap and Palau this upcoming 
week. At Chuuk Lagoon, a NET disturbance over southern Chuuk State
looks to weaken slightly and shift a bit southward Sunday, then
meander northwest into eastern Yap State early next week. Trade- 
wind convergence on the northern side of the NET axis are expected to
maintain periods of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms for
Chuuk for much of the upcoming week. 

Southwest monsoon swell and northwest swell from distant TS Jangmi
are producing 5 to 7 foot seas at Yap and Palau. Meanwhile, trade
swell and light west swell are producing seas of 4 to 5 feet at
Chuuk. As northwest and southwest-west swells gradually diminish,
combined seas are expected to subside to 3 to 4 feet around
Wednesday. Light to moderate southwest to west winds and occasional
fresh to strong gusts continue across Yap and Palau tonight, but 
overall, light to gentle winds will prevail over the next several
days across western Micronesia.
